items.title: Captured Ukrainian-born soldiers tell BBC why they fought for Russia
items.description: Men born in Ukraine who fought for Russia are tried for treason, but at a prisoner of war camp in western Ukraine, many believe they were defending their homeland.

items.title: Kremlin cracks down on all anti-war voices ahead of Russia's elections
items.description: Lev Shlosberg, one of the few Russian opposition figures to publicly denounce the offensive in Ukraine while remaining in Russia, has been sentenced to more than 11 years in prison. His party, the only anti-war political group, has been barred from the September 20 election.

items.title: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees have been stuck at a camp in Qatar since 2021
items.description: More than 1,000 Afghan refugees who fled their homes in 2021 have been stuck in Camp As-Sayliyah, Qatar. They're isolated and unable to leave, despite many having aided U.S. forces during the war.

items.title: Why the US is going after the International Criminal Court
items.description: Marco Rubio, Donald Trump's secretary of state, has announced sanctions against two members of the International Criminal Court, including its president. Rubio's pressure on the court has far-reaching consequences.

items.title: International Criminal Court: New US sanctions ‘a flagrant attack’ against its independence
items.description: The International Criminal Court (ICC) on Wednesday responded to a new round of US sanctions targeting its president and a senior prosecutor, calling them “a flagrant attack” against the court.
